data.narrative:
Reditus Space is a seed-stage space systems company founded by Stef Crum (CEO, PhD in Space Systems Engineering with prior NASA and Space Force orbital operations experience) and Will Sherman (CTO). The company has raised $7.1M to date. The valuation universe comprises 5 public Space & Aerospace peers (RKLB, PL, LUNR, ASTS, SATL) and 8 private comparables including SpaceX, Sierra Space, and Planet Labs.

Of three valuation methods assessed, only stage-progression proved applicable. This method uses the $7.1M total raised as a proxy for current value and applies a 2.5x multiplier typical for seed-to-next-stage progression, yielding $18M. Peer-median triangulation was not feasible: while 11 same-sector private companies exist, none met the narrow filter criteria (same stage, adjacent stage, or similar valuation tier) required for statistical reliability. Public-comp anchoring could not be executed due to absence of revenue data, a standard limitation with private company analysis; the sector P/S median of 23.9x across six public tickers remains inapplicable without this figure.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $15M to $20M, centered at $18M. This range reflects the stage-progression method's single-point output with conservative bounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of revenue or near-term runway metrics, insufficient private-peer comparables at seed stage, and lack of public revenue disclosure from the target. A fuller triangulation would require either disclosed financials or identification of additional seed-stage Space & Aerospace precedents.
